title: Argument Collapse: LLMs Flatten Long-Form Public Debate
reasoning: The paper studies 'argument collapse'—the tendency of LLMs to produce a narrower range of arguments than humans. While the datasets used (NYT and Boston Review) include religious and ethical topics as categories for analysis, the paper focuses on structural and content diversity (uniqueness and recovery rates) rather than benchmarking or evaluating religious traditions, moral judgment, or ethical frameworks themselves.
